msIdentifier.idno: MS Otto F. Ege leaf 8 (part of the previously untraced Wilton Processional)

provenance.orgName: Wilton, Wiltshire. Abbey of St Mary the Virgin and St Edith, of Benedictine nuns
provenance.p: A leaf in the Public Library at Cincinnati, from a processional now largely broken-up into single leaves, includes a litany of saints set to music, in which the virgins are Ywi, Mary Magdalene, Edith, and Agnes, followed immediately by a setting for Edith. Other leaves include references to a "cantrix".

history.provenance: A transcript now at Solesmes was made by Dom Jausions, c. 1860. See G. Benoît-Castelli, 'Un processional anglais du XlVe. S.: Le processional dit de Rollington', Ephemerides liturgica lxxv (1961): 281-326. This was the last known provenance according to the second edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1964).

Around 1948, the manuscript was broken up by Otto F. Ege. See especially Alison Altstatt, 'Re-membering the Wilton Processional', Notes, June 2016, Vol. 72, No. 4 (June 2016), pp. 690-732. The current record, which relates predominantly to the fragment that is now Cincinnati, Public Library, MS Otto F. Ege leaf 8, was added in MLGB3 (2009-2015). More broadly, thirty three further leaves have been traced, which are now widely dispersed. For an itemized list with current locations, see the table in Altstatt 2016, pp. 692-695.

recordHist.source: Neil R. Ker, ed., Medieval Libraries of Great Britain: A List of Surviving Books, Royal Historical Society Guides and Handbooks, 3 (London, 1941; 2nd edn, 1964; supplement, ed. Andrew G. Watson, 1987; digital edn, ed. Richard Sharpe and James M. W. Willoughby, 2010–15).

revisionDesc.change: Record edited to add reference to Altstatt 2016 and consequently further information about how and when the manuscript was broken up, and where other fragments are recorded. Also edited to clarify data history (location reported in different iterations of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain). Added citation to G. Benoît-Castelli from corresponding Medieval Libraries of Great Britain index card.
